answer: Conductance-Bounded Topology Isolation. An agent's receiving capacity is bounded by the network flow passing through its local cluster edge, much like water carving a single river through dense rock. To integrate a new node, the network measures local clustering coefficients and edge-disjoint path redundancy using a crystal lattice analysis of neighbor connectivity. An attacker adding synthetic agents pays a heavy structural cost: to bypass isolation limits without dense external wiring, they must flood every surrounding orchard of legitimate peers with redundant messages,
